findings.message: The new comment says HR is loaded 'never through another module's internals (graph rule R1)', but `installed("hr")` still loads `@amax/hr/module` at runtime. It only builds the template string `import(`@amax/${id}/module`)` from `setup.ts`, and `scripts/graph/rules.mjs` only checks plain string import specifiers. The test does exactly what it did before; R1 just can't see it now. That works here because allocations' `setup.ts` already loads its dependency manifests this way, and that line predates this change. Fix: reword the comment to say the manifest is loaded the way the app's registry loads installed modules, and that R1 only applies to static imports. Don't present this as a fix for the boundary itself.
findings.scenario: A reader trusts the comment and copies `installed("<other>")` into a module's non-test code to read another module's internals. `npm run check:graph` still passes, because the scanner skips template-literal import specifiers.
